stops.note: the art of transmuting metals practised in Roman Egypt, as by Zosimos of Panopolis around 300; the name's origin is disputed (Greek khymos 'juice' or an Egyptian name for Egypt, Kemet)
Arabic added the article al-; writings attributed to Jabir ibn Hayyan made alchemy a major science of the Islamic world
Robert of Chester's Latin translation of 1144 introduced Arabic alchemy to Europe
the al- was dropped for the new science; Robert Boyle's The Sceptical Chymist (1661) attacked the alchemical view of elements

current_meaning: the science of the composition, properties and reactions of substances
